Olga / Laura — read through their redlines. Quick notes from legal triage:
1) 'Exclusive ownership of prompts' — we can agree they own customer-provided prompts and datasets; must carve out safe runtime telemetry and derivative model improvements produced by Redwood (example: general improvements to the hosted model that are not customer-specific). We should avoid wording that allows them to opt-out of improved weights that come from platform-level training.
2) Training opt-in — acceptable as a commercial concession. Propose: customer must opt-in and provide explicit written consent for any model retraining using their data; default is no retraining.
3) Feedback license — propose a limited license to use anonymized feedback/telemetry for product quality and safety improvements, explicitly excluding training for customer-specific models.
4) Evidence list — SOC2 summary ok; procurement will want KMS/HSM binding statement. We can provide a one-page operations attestation (non-audit statement) but not full keys in writing.

Action items:
- Laura: draft counterlanguage for sections 3.2 (Ownership) and 5.1 (Training) with two options (Commercial and Conservative).
- Olga: coordinate with Ethan to get a one-paragraph redline response and lock procurement expectations (signoff triggers).
- Ben: I'll prepare the limited feedback license language and an operations attestation template.

I'll be on the sync at 10:00 tomorrow.

Ben Carter

Thanks — drafting now. Preliminary proposed language below (will send formal redline doc):

Ownership clause (proposed):
- Customer retains ownership of Customer Data and Customer Prompts. Redwood retains ownership of the Redwood Platform, underlying models, and any model weights or improvements arising from aggregated, de-identified usage across customers. No Customer Data or Prompts will be used for model retraining unless Customer provides prior written consent.

Training clause (proposed):
- Any retraining that uses Customer Data or Prompts will require a separate written opt-in. If Customer agrees, Redwood will use standard pseudonymization and aggregation practices and provide a summary of datasets used on request. Customer may request evidence of aggregation steps where feasible.

Feedback license (proposed):
- Customer grants Redwood a limited, worldwide, royalty-free, revocable license to use anonymized feedback and telemetry for the sole purposes of improving platform quality, safety, and general models. This license does not include rights to use Customer Data or Prompts for customer-specific retraining nor confer ownership to outputs produced by Customer.

Attachments to deliver to Procurement: SOC2-summary.pdf, one-page operations attestation (KMS statement), and a short redline response (we'll produce).

I'll circulate the redline doc by EOD for WG review.

Laura Bennett
VP, Legal Operations
Redwood Inference
